subject: 2 steps BYM model: is it possible?

messages.author: cd79aec8f4be0778
messages.subject: 2 steps BYM model: is it possible?
parts:
Dear all,

I would like to carry out a 2 steps spatial model, but I don’t know if it is possible with INLA.

First step:

I want to make a BYM model where I am smoothing a variable (a percentage).

                n~binomial(p,m)

                logit(p)=alpha+spatial+heterogeneous

                with these model we obtain p’, which are the posterior predictive distributions for each area (i.e. spatial smoothed percentages).


Second step:

I want to introduce the posterior predictive distributions as a covariate in another BYM model. I don’t want to introduce the posterior mean of p’ (or another point estimation). I would like to maintain the uncertainty (or variability) of these estimations and incorporate it into the following model.

                Therefore the model more or less:

                O~poisson(E·RR)

                Log(RR)=alpha+spatial+heterogeneous+beta·p’

Finally I would like to obtain the association, i.e. exp(beta) posterior mean and its credible interval.

Thank you for your help!

Marc

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: 2 steps BYM model: is it possible?
parts:
Hi!

The r-inla software cannot handle joint estimation of these kinds of models, since they cannot be (jointly) written on the standard generalised linear regression form (because of the logit-link for p; if the model had beta*logit(p) it could be done with current r-inla).  But they fall under a more general class of "two-stage models" for which it is perhaps possible to construct a general Laplace approximation method, extending the INLA method.

/Finn
